messages:
oliver: Hey team — hitting a tricky one in production today. Flask app (gunicorn, 4 workers) using redwood-py sync wrapper. Intermittent RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop + a short spike of 401s from the API followed by retries. Started after upgrading to redwood-py 0.4.0 and httpx 0.23.3. Repro steps below.

oliver: Repro (minimal):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..)  # using sync wrapper
def handler():
    r = client.chat.create(...)
    return r.text
```
Running under gunicorn w/ sync workers. Stack excerpt: 
```
RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/sync.py", line 72, in sync_call
    return asyncio.run(coro)
```
Also seeing short burst of 401s in logs: "401 Unauthorized - token invalid" then SDK retries and succeeds. Not sure if they're related. :confused:

support-bot: Thanks for the report — see docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/python#sync-wrapper ; tagging support for handoff :rotating_light:

mike: @oliver can you paste exact versions: `redwood-py`, `httpx`, `uvloop` (if used), gunicorn worker class? Also are you using any thread/greenlet worker like gevent?

oliver: versions: redwood-py 0.4.0, httpx 0.23.3, python 3.10, gunicorn 20.1.0, worker class default sync. No gevent/uvloop configured.

anya: Two quick thoughts: 1) sync wrapper in 0.4.0 still calls `asyncio.run()` on each call which conflicts if the process already has a running loop (e.g., spawned by embedding frameworks). 2) the 401 spike could be a token-refresh race: multiple concurrent requests try to refresh creds and one wins, others get short 401 then succeed after retry.

mike: agree with @anya. In multi-threaded/high-concurrency WSGI setups the sync wrapper can be unsafe. For Flask+gunicorn sync workers you usually get separate processes so it should be fine, but if you spawn threads or use a library that starts a loop, collision happens.

oliver: interesting — we don't intentionally start any loops. This only showed up after bumping redwood-py. Could the SDK start an internal background loop?

anya: Not background loop, but see bug report where `sync.py` did `asyncio.run()` unguarded in some code paths. Fix in 0.4.2 replaces `asyncio.run` with `anyio.from_thread.run` when available and adds a loop existence check. Try pinning to 0.4.2 if you can.

eng-oncall: Also for the 401s: check if you're sharing a single client instance across threads without a lock during token refresh. If token refresh in the SDK isn't fully thread-safe for that release, you'll see transient 401s with immediate retries. Workarounds: 1) use one client per thread/process, 2) upgrade to patched SDK, or 3) add a short jitter to retry/backoff to avoid thundering.

oliver: ok i'll try 0.4.2 and spin one client per worker. Quick question: how do we check the SDK's token refresh log? Where are those logs emitted?

mike: The SDK emits debug logs for auth if you set `logging.getLogger('redwood.auth').setLevel(logging.DEBUG)`. It will show refresh attempts + outcomes.

oliver: pasted small snippet from production logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-18T14:12:03Z] redwood.auth DEBUG: token expiry 1678s, refreshing=false
[2026-02-18T14:12:04Z] redwood.auth INFO: starting refresh
[2026-02-18T14:12:04Z] httpx ERROR: 401 Unauthorized - /v1/chat
[2026-02-18T14:12:04Z] redwood.auth INFO: refresh complete, new token acquired
[2026-02-18T14:12:04Z] httpx INFO: retrying request (attempt 2)
```
That lines up with your theory.

anya: yep — that looks like a race where a request hit just as token rotated. After refresh the retries succeed. With many concurrent in-flight requests you can see a short burst.

eng-oncall: Actions: 1) try `pip install redwood-py==0.4.2 httpx==0.24.0` in staging, 2) ensure one client per worker, 3) enable `redwood.auth` debug logs and repro with a load test (wrk/hey) to verify no 401 spike. If it persists, collect `--trace` httpx logs and we'll escalate.

oliver: thanks — will test upgrade + per-worker client today and report back. If upgrade fixes both the eventloop error and 401 bursts, we'll roll to prod. :thumbsup:

mike: if you can't upgrade immediately, quick interim workaround: wrap calls using `anyio.from_thread.run` in your code to ensure the sync adapter doesn't call `asyncio.run` directly (adds complexity but buys time).

support-bot: If you run into full repro, please open a support ticket with logs and set priority high. We'll keep an eye. :eyes:

oliver: opened ticket #SUP-8421 and attached logs. I'll update once staging results are in. Thanks all!
